title: Grounded research desk
tagline: Answers that cite the exact passage, or say they cannot.
summary: Analysts ask questions of a governed corpus and receive answers in which every claim links to a retrieved passage the asker is allowed to read. Unsupported questions are refused, not guessed.
customer_job: Find a defensible answer in policies, research reports and filings without reading forty documents.
baseline: Analysts search shared drives and intranet pages, read in full, and paste excerpts into notes; answers vary by analyst and sources are rarely recorded.
accepted_result: An answer the analyst forwards without rework, with each claim traceable to a passage they are permitted to see.

primary_metric.name: Accepted cited answers per analyst hour
primary_metric.definition: Answers marked forwarded or reused without edit, divided by analyst hours spent in the workspace.

economics.basis: Illustrative assumption for a 120-analyst team; replace with measured volume and baseline time before any business case.

components.label: Research workspace
components.detail: Ask box, cited answer, passage viewer, flag action.

components.label: Workforce sign-in
components.detail: SSO with group claims mapped to document permissions.

components.label: Answer API
components.detail: Authorizes, scopes the corpus by permission, enforces a per-question budget.
components.failure_mode: Retrieval runs without the caller's permission filter.

components.label: Model gateway
components.detail: Routing, fallback, budget, cache and token logs.

components.label: Generation model
components.detail: Writes only from supplied passages and returns passage IDs per claim.
components.failure_mode: Claims a fact with no passage ID.

components.label: Hybrid retrieval index
components.detail: Keyword and vector search with permission tags on every chunk.
components.failure_mode: Stale chunk served after the source changed.

components.label: Ingestion pipeline
components.detail: Parse, chunk, embed and copy source permissions to each chunk.

components.label: Source corpus
components.detail: Versioned documents with owners and review dates.

components.label: Answer ledger
components.detail: Question, answer, passage IDs, model, cost and feedback.

components.label: Traces and cost
components.detail: Latency, tokens, cache hits and refusals per team.

components.label: Eval harness
components.detail: Frozen question set with expected passages and must-refuse cases.

journey.title: Ask under your own identity
journey.narration: The analyst signs in once. The workspace sends the question with a scope token derived from their groups.

journey.title: Retrieve only what they may read
journey.narration: The API filters the index by the caller's permissions before ranking. A passage the analyst cannot open never reaches the model.

journey.title: Write from passages, not memory
journey.narration: The gateway routes a prompt that contains only retrieved passages. The model must return a passage ID for every claim.

journey.title: Answer, or refuse plainly
journey.narration: Claims without a passage are removed. If nothing survives, the workspace shows a refusal with the closest documents to read.

journey.title: Keep the corpus current
journey.narration: A changed document is re-parsed and re-indexed with its permissions. Answers that cited the old version are marked for review.

journey.title: Prove it on every release
journey.narration: The harness replays frozen questions and must-refuse cases. Cost and latency are read from gateway telemetry, not estimated.

evals.method: Negative set built from questions owners confirmed are unanswerable.

evals.method: Gateway telemetry over the frozen set.

gcp.headline: Agent Search with Gemini 3.8 Flash on Cloud Run
gcp.notes: Agent Search handles hybrid retrieval and permission-aware indexing; RAG Engine covers custom chunking. Keep the corpus in Cloud Storage with object-level IAM mirrored into index metadata.
gcp.rationale: Managed retrieval with permission controls and residency options; index and model tie the workload to Agent Platform, which raises exit cost.

vercel.headline: Next.js, AI Gateway and Neon pgvector
vercel.notes: Fastest route to a working desk. Retrieval is yours to build on pgvector with row-level permission filters; AI Gateway gives model choice and fallbacks without a second SDK.
vercel.rationale: Model and data layers stay swappable; enterprise identity, residency and audit depend on the chosen Marketplace partners.

cloudflare.headline: Workers, AI Search and AI Gateway behind Access
cloudflare.notes: AI Search indexes R2 and serves hybrid retrieval through a binding; Access supplies SSO in front of the workspace. Permission filters need metadata on each indexed item.
cloudflare.rationale: Edge latency and low request cost; AI Search is remote-only in development and its permission model must be validated per corpus.

aws.headline: Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Claude on Bedrock
aws.notes: Managed knowledge base handles ingestion and retrieval; metadata filters carry permissions. Claude on Bedrock keeps traffic inside the account boundary.
aws.rationale: Strong account-level controls; more services to wire than the primary platforms.

azure.headline: Azure AI Search with Foundry Models
azure.notes: Security trimming in Azure AI Search with Entra groups is the natural permission model for Microsoft 365 estates.
azure.rationale: Best fit where documents already live in SharePoint and identity is Entra; search unit pricing is step-shaped.

railway.headline: Containers, Postgres pgvector and a direct model API
railway.notes: All parts are yours: chunking, permission filters, budgets and retries. Suits a small team that wants full control and one bill per vendor.
railway.rationale: Lowest lock-in; identity, audit and guardrails are custom work.
